gloss: the underworld; land of the dead

definitions.gloss: the underworld; land of the dead (Japanese mythology)
definitions.explanation: The land of the dead in Japanese mythology, usually called {黄泉|よみ}の{国|くに}. In the Kojiki, the god Izanagi goes there to bring back his dead wife Izanami and flees in horror.

examples.english: To go to the land of the dead.

examples.japanese: イザナギ⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{黄泉|よみ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{国|くに}→国：02204_kuni⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧{逃|に}げ{帰|かえ}った。
examples.english: Izanagi fled back from the land of the dead.

examples.japanese: 「よみがえる」⟦という→という：09577_toiu⟧⟦{言葉|ことば}→言葉：02880_kotoba⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、{黄泉|よみ}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{帰|かえ}る→帰る：00508_kaeru⟧こと⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{由来|ゆらい}→由来：05451_yurai⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦される→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: The word yomigaeru (to come back to life) is said to come from returning from Yomi.

notes:
Written with the Chinese characters for "yellow springs," a Chinese name for the underworld, and given the native reading よみ.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {黄泉|よみ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{国|くに}→国：02204_kuni⟧: the land of the dead
- {黄泉路|よみじ}: the road to the land of the dead
- {黄泉|よみ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{客|きゃく}→客：00865_kyaku⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧: to die (literary; literally "become a guest of Yomi")

ETYMOLOGY:
The verb ⟦{蘇|よみがえ}る→蘇る：04004_yomigaeru⟧ (to come back to life) is traditionally explained as {黄泉|よみ} + ⟦{帰|かえ}る→帰る：00508_kaeru⟧, "to return from Yomi."

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{冥土|めいど}→冥土：22009_meido⟧: the Buddhist world of the dead
- ⟦あの{世|よ}→あの世：10214_anoyo⟧: the other world — the everyday expression
